newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Republicans ask Rubin for tax cut details.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Republicans ask Rubin for tax cut details.

text.p: The chairmen of the House and Senate committees that oversee tax law on Tuesday asked Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin to provide details of the Clinton administration's broad tax cut plan.

House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer, a Texas Republican, and Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth, a Delaware Republican, said in a letter to Rubin that unless the administration provided legal language, they could not analyze the impact of the plan.
President Clinton's 1998 budget proposes a $98 billion tax cut over the next five years to help middle-class families with children, promote higher education and encourage savings.
Many of the tax provisions would sunset at the end of 2000. The lawmakers said they needed more precise information about the sunset in order to analyze the tax plan.
"The American people won't know if the administration is proposing a tax hike or tax reduction until Congress is provided with this information," the letter said.
